description: A search-filter-sort spec is valid when the entity is declared, all filter types are from the allowed set, sort entries declare a default direction, no-results and loading states are handled, filter persistence is explicit, and all ids are unique.

rules.description: search-filter-sort-spec.json must exist with entity (string), filters (array), and sorts (array). Specs without these fields cannot be validated.
Every filter must declare id, label, and type. Filters without these fields cannot be rendered or referenced by the search engine.
Every sort must declare id, label, and field. Sorts without a field binding cannot generate an API sort parameter.
Every filter.type must be one of: text, select, multi-select, range, date-range, boolean, tag. Unknown filter types produce undefined UI behavior.

Spec must declare noResultsState with message and at least one of clearFiltersAction or suggestionsEnabled, or set noResultsHandledGlobally:true. Search results that return nothing must communicate what to do next.
Every sort entry must declare defaultDirection as asc or desc. Sorts without a declared direction create inconsistent initial render order.
Spec must declare loadingState with type skeleton, spinner, or progressive, or set loadingHandledGlobally:true. Search results that load without feedback create perceived unresponsiveness.
Spec must declare persistence as session, url, none, or user-preference. Filters without a persistence policy reset unexpectedly on navigation or page reload.
All filter ids must be unique within the spec. Duplicate filter ids create conflicting state keys and unpredictable behavior.
